data.assessment: Under rush load the town delivered 216.6 of 228 orders on time with nothing unfinished, so the losses are about 11.4 late deliveries, 10.0 of them pickup-deadline misses. Blocking is the main friction: 1824 s town-wide, concentrated on A (843 s, rate 0.94) and B (756 s, rate 0.93). C is barely blocked (225 s) and carries almost all sanctions (11.0), which suggests C's parked robots are what block the others. The 16 release overstays and only 3 blocking-guard evictions suggest the guard threshold of 3 waiting robots rarely fires before damage is done.

proposals.title: Lower blocking_guard threshold block_k 3 -> 2
proposals.rationale: Blocked time is 1824 s, mostly borne by A (843 s) and B (756 s), and pickup misses (10.0) dominate the late deliveries. Evicting a parked robot once 2 robots wait behind it should cut blocking and recover some of the ~11 late orders, raising on_time_deliveries and the weakest rate (B 0.93). What changed since period 1 is the rush environment, where blocking is far larger. A should vote yes; C (sanctions 11.0) will likely lose utility from more Major evictions and vote no; B is uncertain because it both suffers blocking and parks on the road (48.8 waits). If it measures well but fails the vote, that is the override question already passed to the regulator, not a reason to adopt by other means.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
assumptions: C's parked robots cause most of the blocking that A and B suffer, inferred from C's low blocked seconds and high sanctions.
Evicted robots clear the intersection quickly enough to shorten other companies' pickup times.
The mode stays fixed at DISTRIBUTED, so the transition thresholds have no effect.
unknowns: Whether period 1's rejected option 1 was this same block_k change; its utility pattern (C falling sharply) suggests it was.
Whether the extra evictions cost the evicted robots time on their own next orders.
How B's utility nets out between fewer blockages and its own evictions.

regulation_proposals.title: Lower vote quorum from 2 to 1
regulation_proposals.rationale: In period 1 a measured customer gain (+9.2 on-time, weakest rate 0.84 -> 0.98) was blocked only by the B and C votes, and the same pattern is likely again for block_k. With quorum 1, an amendment would pass if one company supports it and it also clears the on-time improvement gate (>= 1.0) and the invariants. Customers would gain fewer late deliveries when such amendments exist. Each company loses its blocking minority: C, which parks most and is sanctioned most, is the likeliest to be outvoted and lose utility, and B could be outvoted when it parks; A could likewise be overruled on changes that hurt it. The safeguards that remain are the improvement gate, the min_company_on_time_rate floor of 0.6 and max_unfinished of 2, but none of these protects a company's utility.
assumptions: Future amendments that pass the improvement gate are generally good for customers.
The objective gate and the invariants are enough protection against harmful single-company proposals.
unknowns: Whether companies would change behavior, or stop cooperating, once they lose the veto.
Whether the regulator prefers a narrower fix, such as letting a human override specific failed votes, over a standing lower quorum.
The exact effect on the block_k proposal, which depends on how it measures.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Only through amendments that clear the gate but fail the vote under quorum 2, such as period 1's option 1.

predictions.subject: metric:sanction_total
predictions.note: Amendments that tighten road rules are more likely to pass.

predictions.subject: metric:utility_gap
predictions.note: C's utility is likely to fall relative to A's.
